# Application states and transitions

This is the state model the dashboard, the queue runner and the reconciliation
tools share. The register (`state/applications.csv`) is the only record of an
application. The queue is work to do; a finished queue row is not a state.

## The states

| State | Meaning | Who sets it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `QUEUED` | In the apply queue. Nothing has been prepared or sent. | discovery, the dashboard, a retry |
| `DRAFTING` | The advert is saved and preparation has started, but there are no gated documents yet. Shown for a queue row that has an ad, keywords or grounding. | preparation |
| `PREPARED` | The CV (and a letter only when required) is generated, measured and gate-PASS. Ready to submit. | a review/prepare run |
| `SUBMITTED` | The application was sent and confirmed, with a matching provenance row. An ATS status such as Under Consideration stays here: it is still waiting, not a new stage. | `record_submission.py`, or an approved email with the documents |
| `IN_PROGRESS` | An active process step is underway: an assessment, background checks, or a live recruiter conversation. Mere employer review stays `SUBMITTED`. | reconciliation, a manual update |
| `INTERVIEW` | An interview is invited, scheduled or held. Its sub-state says which. | reconciliation, a manual update |

| `OFFER` | An offer was received. | a manual update |
| `REJECTED` | The employer declined. | reconciliation, a manual update |
| `BLOCKED` | A wall stopped the run: a CAPTCHA or login, a gate failure, a missing advert, an email-only ATS, or an unclear eligibility rule. It is work for you, not a rejection. | the runner or the agent, with the exact reason |
| `MANUAL` | A human-owned lead or step: an intro meeting, a network row, a recruiter email with no advert. | `email_opportunities.py`, a manual update |
| `CLOSED` | The role is not applicable: not eligible, expired, withdrawn or a duplicate. The sub-state says which. | the runner, `prepare_role.py`, a manual update |

There is no `NO RESULT` application state. A run that cannot produce an
application records `BLOCKED` or `CLOSED` with the exact reason. A finished
queue row that never became a register row is a **queue leftover**, not an
application; see below.

`INTERVIEW` rows also carry **`interview_stage`** in the register: `screen`,
`hiring-manager`, `technical`, `panel`, `final` or `offer` (empty when not
recorded). The sub-state says *what is happening* (invited, scheduled, today,
held); the stage says *which round* it is. The drawer records it without
changing the status, and the grid shows it as a small chip.

## The normal path

```
QUEUED -> DRAFTING -> PREPARED -> SUBMITTED -> IN_PROGRESS -> INTERVIEW -> OFFER
                                      |                            |
                                      +-> BLOCKED / CLOSED          +-> REJECTED
```

`SUBMITTED` is the handoff from the candidate to the employer. `IN_PROGRESS` is
not set by a successful submit; it means an active step has started: an
assessment, background checks, or a live conversation. A silent employer, or an
ATS label such as Under Consideration, keeps the row at `SUBMITTED` and its
sub-state (`awaiting`, `acknowledged`, `stale`, `assessment`).

## Branch rules

- **QUEUED or DRAFTING -> BLOCKED** when the run hits a wall before it can
  prepare a usable application: a missing or dead advert, an unclear location or
  work model, a failed alignment/fill/pre-submit gate, a login/CAPTCHA, or an
  email-only application that the browser cannot send.
- **PREPARED -> SUBMITTED** only after a real confirmation and a provenance row.
  A submit click alone is not enough.
- **PREPARED -> BLOCKED or CLOSED** when the submission cannot happen: a wall,
  or a posting that expired or was filled.
- **Any active state -> CLOSED** when the role is withdrawn, expired, not
  eligible, or a duplicate.
- **BLOCKED -> QUEUED** when you retry or re-queue it. That is the only way back
  into the apply path.
- **MANUAL -> QUEUED, PREPARED or CLOSED** when the human decides what the lead
  is worth. `MANUAL` is never a silent waiting state.
- A network or email-only row has no apply URL. It can be prepared or have a
  draft email, but it is not submitted through a browser. **Prepare and submit**
  is offered only when the row has a real URL; otherwise use **Prepare
  documents** and the email route.

## Reposts and second attempts

One row is kept per company and role. A repost reuses that row:

- Preparation for the new attempt records `PREPARED`, even when the earlier
  attempt is `IN_PROGRESS` or `SUBMITTED`. The register refuses a live-to-
  `PREPARED` write unless the review is an explicit repost (`--repost`); a plain
  document refresh leaves the live status alone and notes the new files.
- The note keeps the earlier status and date, for example
  `repost: earlier application still IN_PROGRESS since 2026-10-08; new documents
  prepared, not submitted`. The live recruiter thread is not lost.
- A submission run does **not** reset `PREPARED` to `QUEUED`. The grid shows a
  spinner while the run is live, and the outcome sets `SUBMITTED`, `BLOCKED` or
  `CLOSED` directly. A crash leaves the row at `PREPARED`, which is the truth.

## Employer application caps

A cap is per employer, not per role. A role refused because the employer
already has three applications in 90 days (or two in 30) is `CLOSED`, with
the dashboard sub-state `employer cap`; it is never `SUBMITTED`, because
nothing was sent. `state/employer-limits.json` stops the runner from trying
again until the date passes.

## Queue leftovers

`state/queue.done` records that a queue row finished. If no register row was
created, the row is a leftover: work was attempted, but there is no application
to track. It is not an application state and must not appear in the state map.

```bash
python3 tools/queue_leftovers.py --write        # list them in state/queue-leftovers.md
python3 tools/queue_leftovers.py --drop         # remove them from the active queue
```

The active queue should contain only work to do. A row that is already in
`queue.done`, or whose register row is `SUBMITTED`, `IN_PROGRESS`, `INTERVIEW`,
`OFFER`, `REJECTED`, `CLOSED`, `BLOCKED` or `MANUAL`, is not pending. Clean it
with:

```bash
python3 tools/queue_clean.py --apply
```

`--drop` also moves their `queue.done` entries to `state/queue-leftovers.done`,
so the register audit stays honest. The full queue rows are kept in
`state/queue-leftovers.tsv` and every artifact stays on disk. Append a row from
that file to `state/queue.tsv` to re-queue it, or leave it closed.

## The state map

The **Application states** panel draws this model: the normal path, the
BLOCKED/MANUAL branches, SCAMS and SHELVED side nodes, and the REJECTED/CLOSED
terminals. The bucket chips are views of the same rows, not extra states.
`SCAMS` and `SHELVED` are overlays: they never replace the register status.

# Storage
Jobsquirrel · Docs
The pipeline keeps a lot of machine-local data, and most of it compresses hard: run logs, the Gmail body cache, and the GraphRAG indexing cache. None of it is committed; it lives only on your machine. python3 tools/storage.py # report: what is using space python3 tools/storage.py --logs # gzip logs idle for a day python3 tools/storage.py --pack-log X.log # gzip one finished transcript python3 tools/storage.py --state # pack cold per-role artifacts python3 tools/storage.py --hydrate-all # restore everything, in place python3 tools/storage.py --hydrate acme-eng # restore one role's artifacts python3 tools/storage.py --gmail-cache # gzip state/gmail_cache.json python3 tools/storage.py --graphrag-cache # dry run: what archiving saves python3 tools/storage.py --all --apply # everything, including the archive ## What each action does **`--logs`** gzips `state/logs/*.log|*.out|*.err` that have not been touched for a day, and `kb/graphrag/logs/` after 2 days (an indexing run finishes in hours, so a two-day-old index log is idle). A log being written right now is never moved, and the append-only logs are excluded by name (`dashboard-chat.log`, `dashboard-action.log`, `approval.log`, `run_queue.out`, `linkedin_run.out`, `human_assist.out`, `reconcile.log`, `camoufox_server*.log`): gzipping one of those would corrupt it on the next append. Override the window with `--days`. **`--pack-log PATH`** gzips one specific log immediately. The queue runners call it as soon as a role finishes, so a run's transcript is history the moment the role is done, rather than a day later. The two logs that really are appended to are capped instead: when `dashboard-chat.log` or `dashboard-action.log` passes 2 MB, the dashboard rolls it to `dashboard-chat-.log.gz` and restarts the live file empty, so yesterday's transcript is kept (and still listed as a task log) without an unbounded plain file. The dashboard reads both forms: `foo.log.gz` still appears as task `foo`. **`--state`** packs the per-role artifacts: `state/job-descriptions/`, `state/ats/`, `state/kb-context/`, `state/cv-content/`, `state/letters-content/`, `state/gates/` and the register digest: once they are older than the window (7 days by default, `--state-days` overrides it). They are text, so they shrink 2-4x; a fresh artifact from today's run is left alone. Packing is invisible because `tools/stateio.py` resolves `x` or `x.gz` for every reader: `jd_guard`, `ats_keywords`, `kb_graphrag`, `check_alignment`, `cv_target`, `check_documents`, `gate_receipt` (a packed receipt still satisfies `record_submission`), and the dashboard, which reads the packed twin rather than restoring it: browsing the grid never undoes the saving. Anything that needs a real file calls `stateio.ensure()`, which restores it in place and keeps the artifact's original age. A queue run restores everything at the start (`--hydrate-all`) so the runner and the agent always see plain paths, and packs the cold leftovers when it finishes. To restore by hand: `--hydrate-all`, or `--hydrate ` for one role. Two things are deliberately never packed: files that are appended to or written by shell redirection (`queue*.tsv`, `*.done`, `*.csv`, `state/drafts/`), and symlinks (some older role keys are links to the canonical slug). **Files git tracks are left plain by default.** Packing one shows up as a deletion plus an untracked `.gz`, and every pack/hydrate cycle would churn the repo; git already zlib-compresses blobs and delta-packs them, so `git gc` handles that side. `--include-tracked` overrides it if you have untracked the per-role artifacts on purpose (for example after `git rm --cached` them). **`--gmail-cache`** gzips `state/gmail_cache.json` (roughly 9x smaller). The cache holds decoded message bodies keyed by id; it is derived data and can be deleted at any time. `gmail_reconcile.py` and `gmail_review_model.py` read either form, and `save_cache` keeps the compressed form when that is what it finds, so the next reconcile does not re-inflate it. **`--graphrag-cache`** tars `kb/graphrag/cache/` into `kb/archives/graphrag-cache-.tar.zst` and removes the loose files (roughly 6x smaller). This cache only speeds up (re)indexing: queries read `kb/graphrag/output/`, so retrieval keeps working without it, and the archive is restorable if you would rather keep the incremental-index history: python3 tools/storage.py --graphrag-cache --apply tar -C kb/graphrag -xf kb/archives/graphrag-cache-.tar.zst \ --use-compress-program=unzstd It is a dry run unless you pass `--apply`, because it is the only action that moves a large directory. ## What is not compressed `documents/` holds `.docx` and `.pdf`, which are already compressed container formats; re-packing them saves nothing and breaks the files. The GraphRAG `output/` directory (LanceDB tables + parquet) is read at query time and must stay unpacked. `.git/` is git's own compression problem, and a checkout that has been committing documents for weeks slowly fills with loose objects. One command reclaims it: git gc --prune=now # 118 MB -> 36 MB in a typical busy checkout `tools/storage.py` does not run it for you: it rewrites the object database, so it is a git decision, not a file-compression one. ## Backups and the data lifecycle `tools/backup.py` (Settings → **Backup & data**) is the other half of storage: `--state`/`--logs` shrink what is there, a backup lets you move or rebuild it. A backup zip holds `config/`, `answers/`, `kb/sources/`, `state/` (minus logs and the mail cache) and optionally `documents/`; the GraphRAG index is excluded because it is rebuildable from the sources. Anything destructive (restore or clear) writes an automatic safety copy to `backups/` first (`pre-restore-*.zip`, `pre-clear-*.zip`), and only the newest five of those are kept. Your own `jobsquirrel-*.zip` backups are never pruned. `backups/` is git-ignored: it contains personal data. ## Checking `python3 tools/doctor.py` includes a `storage` line with the current sizes of logs, the Gmail cache and the GraphRAG cache, plus what compression could reclaim right now. `tests/test_storage.py` covers the log and cache round-trips and the dashboard's compressed-log reader.

You drive the whole thing by **talking to your agent in plain English**. `AGENTS.md` teaches it the procedures; you set direction with short goals. You never run the tools by hand, but you can watch everything it does. ## The rhythm ``` discover → (optionally review) → apply → monitor → reconcile → repeat ``` A normal session: find roles, queue them, run the pipeline, keep an eye on progress, then reconcile replies and clear anything that needs a human. ## Typical prompts You don't need special syntax, just say what you want. The regex classifier is fast but language-specific, so clearly job-related mail can still land in OTHER. The triage layer checks ATS and company sender domains, application/requisition ids, meeting links with dates, LinkedIn job alerts and system senders, then marks the item as **job-related** with a category hint. - Open the Gmail review and choose **triage: job-related** to see only those messages. - The hint is review-only: it never changes a status or sends anything. - Personal or local domain additions go in `config/email-triage.json`; the public template is `config/email-triage.example.json`. ## State model: the application state machine The application process is a **state machine**. The register keeps a small, stable set of **statuses**: the machine stage used by the pre-submit gates, the queue and the reconciler - and one row moves through them (`QUEUED → DRAFTING → PREPARED → SUBMITTED → IN_PROGRESS → INTERVIEW → OFFER`, with `BLOCKED`/`MANUAL` branches and `REJECTED`/`CLOSED` terminals). The dashboard draws that machine above the grid and every tool reads and writes the same state. On top of each status the dashboard derives a **sub-state** from the role's notes and follow-up flag. The sub-state is the human answer to “what is actually happening, and what should I do next?”. - **Knowledge graph navigation:** the arrows in the Knowledge toolbar go back and forward through graph views (Alt+Left / Alt+Right). - **Columns:** right-click a column header to show or hide columns. The choice is remembered. Drag a divider to resize a column; double-click it to reset that column. - The **Status** cell shows the status chip and, underneath, the sub-state when it adds detail. - **Filters → any sub-state** narrows the grid to one sub-state; like a group, it crosses the bucket boundaries. - The **top row of the grid** carries the bucket filter chips (Active, Focus, Needs you, Probably scams, Prepared, Ongoing, To apply, Done, All) with live counts, plus the live status and run controls. Click a state to clear the search and the other filters, expand its sub-states and filter to it, then click a sub-state to narrow further. A scam marker on a grid row, or a red/amber banner in the role drawer or the Gmail review, means: **read it before you reply.** > **Never download or install software, join a chat-only interview, share a wallet, > seed phrase or private key, pay a fee, or move money during a recruitment process.** The common high-risk signals are remote-access tools ("install AnyDesk before the interview"), wallet/seed-phrase requests, pay-to-work fees, equipment cheques, chat-only interviews on Telegram/WhatsApp, and unrealistic pay for no experience. A HIGH signal stops document preparation; the role can still be recorded `BLOCKED` with the reason. Mail is checked too: the sender domain against the company's apply domain (lookalikes), free mailboxes, Reply-To mismatches, installers, shortened/IP/punycode links, wallet-connect links and dangerous attachments. It uses one toolbar for the title, the **Universe** / **Map** toggle, search, view controls and actions. **Universe** shows the whole graph as theme islands; **Map** drills through **Topics** (ontology classes), **Communities** (the generated hierarchy), **Entities** and **Ego** networks. Click an entity for its description, sources, neighbours and strongest connections; double-click opens its ego network. Selecting an entity lights its neighbourhood and dims the rest, then fades back after a few seconds; clicking empty space restores the previous view. **Ask** answers questions with citations, **Semantic** searches entities by meaning, and **role evidence** maps a saved ad's keywords to grounded evidence and gaps. **Sources** uploads/deletes/rebuilds documents, **Add** records a fact or skill without a rebuild, and **Roles** opens a role in the application drawer (or prepares a queued role). Drag to orbit, scroll to zoom, right-drag to pan. The full guide is **[KNOWLEDGE-GRAPH.md](KNOWLEDGE-GRAPH.md)**. The graph and the application drawer share the same evidence: a claim you add under **Add** is appended to every GraphRAG context immediately and appears in the graph view through a live skill overlay, so no rebuild is needed - re-prepare the role to fold it into the CV. Rebuild only when you change a document under Sources. A role you open under **Roles** uses the same grounding and gates as a queue run. ## Backup, restore and start over Settings → **Backup & data** covers the three things you do around the edges of a job search: take a copy, put a copy back, or clear the system and start again. **Backup** writes one `.zip` with everything the pipeline cannot regenerate: `config/` (profile, CV, archetypes, mail/calendar and Google settings), `answers/`, `kb/sources/` (your corpus), `state/` (register, queues, provenance, drafts, saved ads, keyword files, grounding and content packs, gate receipts) and, unless you untick it, `documents/` (rendered CVs, letters, and the exact files you sent). Transcripts, the mail cache and the GraphRAG index are left out: they are noise or rebuildable. python3 tools/backup.py create # -> backups/jobsquirrel-.zip python3 tools/backup.py create --no-documents # ~5 MB instead of ~150 MB python3 tools/backup.py list python3 tools/backup.py inspect backups/.zip > **Careful:** the zip holds **your personal data**: CV, applications, and any Google > client secret in `config/google.json`. Keep it private; `backups/` is > git-ignored for that reason. **Restore** replaces `config/`, `state/`, `documents/` and `kb/sources/` with the zip's contents. It asks you to type `RESTORE`, refuses while a queue run is in progress, and **writes a safety backup first**, so a wrong choice is recoverable: python3 tools/backup.py restore backups/.zip --yes **Clear** deletes the pipeline's data and keeps your identity: the register, queues, drafts, saved ads, keyword files, grounding packs and every generated document go; `config/` and `kb/sources/` stay. *Full reset* additionally drops the GraphRAG index (a rebuild takes 20-30 minutes). It asks you to type `CLEAR` and takes a safety backup first: python3 tools/backup.py clear --scope data --yes python3 tools/backup.py clear --scope full --yes Automatic pre-restore/pre-clear copies live in `backups/` and the newest five are kept; your own backups are never pruned. **What the agent will interrupt you for:** a CAPTCHA/2FA/bot check, an email to approve before sending, a verification link or code, an ambiguous eligibility or accuracy rule, or a model budget/rate-limit stop. A handy catch-all prompt: > *"Give me a status: what's running, what's done, what needs me, and roughly > what it's cost so far."* ## Keeping it cheap while you use it - Prefer **REVIEW** and **LIGHT** modes while you tune; they skip the browser and per-role generation. - Keep a **single long agent session** so context stays cacheable. - See [AGENT-SETUP.md](AGENT-SETUP.md) §3-4 for the model choice and cost figures.

# Workflow
Jobsquirrel · Docs
There are two ways to work a role: **manually** (fine-grained control) or via the **queue runner** (`run_queue.sh`), which does the same steps per job automatically. Both rely on the same gates, so the automation never sends anything a human run wouldn't. > Day-to-day, you drive this by prompting an agent in plain English and watching > it work, see **[USING-IT.md](USING-IT.md)** for typical prompts and how to > monitor a run. ## Per-role procedure ``` # 1. Save the ad text, then scan it for recruitment-scam signals. # HIGH means stop: record BLOCKED and do not prepare documents. $EDITOR state/job-descriptions/.md python3 tools/scam_check.py --jd state/job-descriptions/.md --key # 2. Extract ATS keywords python3 tools/ats_keywords.py --jd state/job-descriptions/.md --out state/ats/.txt # 3. Choose the aligned CV archetype and verify python3 tools/check_alignment.py --cv documents/archetypes/_CV_.docx \ --jd state/job-descriptions/.md # must print RESULT: PASS - alignment # 4. Build a targeted CV (ATS-safe .docx + styled .pdf) and a per-role letter. # Ground every claim in state/kb-context/.md (GraphRAG) + config/cv.json. python3 tools/cv_target.py --key --content state/cv-content/.json --require-fill # ...then render the letter (see tools/make_letter.py / cv_builder.render_motivation) # 5. PRE-SUBMIT GATE: nothing is uploaded until this prints RESULT: PASS. # --record writes a hash-stamped receipt; record_submission.py (step 7) # REFUSES to record SUBMITTED without it. Gate the files you will upload. python3 tools/check_documents.py --letter documents/applications/.docx \ --cv documents/applications/.docx --company "" \ --ats-keywords state/ats/.txt --record # (add --engagement contract only for genuine contract/consulting roles) # 6. Apply through the employer's own ATS with the Camoufox browser python3 tools/camoufox_server.py --port 9872 & python3 tools/camoufox_browser.py --server http://127.0.0.1:9872 nav "" # fill, upload, answer questions honestly, submit (see docs/ATS-RECIPES.md) # 7. Record the exact files sent (snapshots + hashes) and upsert the register python3 tools/record_submission.py --company "" --role "" --ats \ --url --cv documents/applications/.docx \ --letter documents/applications/.docx --status SUBMITTED \ --evidence "" ``` ## Queue runner ```bash PARALLEL=3 bash tools/run_queue.sh # processes state/queue.tsv ``` For each row it: checks eligibility against `config/profile.md`; picks and verifies the aligned archetype; builds a targeted CV + letter; runs the pre-submit gate; submits via Camoufox; and records the outcome (or the blocker). Finished rows are appended to `state/queue.done` under the row's **key** (the same identity stored in the register; rows written before that column existed fall back to `company|role`). `LIGHT=1 FIXED_CV=` runs a cheaper mode with one fixed CV, `REVIEW=1` builds and gates the documents without sending, and `PREPARED=1` submits documents that are already gated. **Do not apply twice.** The runner skips a role already applied to (same company and role) with `SKIP-APPLIED`; set `ALLOW_REPOST=1` only for a deliberate second attempt. `python3 tools/queue_prune.py --apply` parks finished rows in `state/queue-parked.tsv`, and `state/employer-limits.json` stops a role at an employer that caps applications (Ashby three per 90 days, for example). Manage caps with `tools/employer_limit.py`. **Seniority first.** When several roles are pending, the runner applies to the most senior first, e.g. a company's *Director of Engineering* before its *Platform Engineer*. Rank (high→low): Chief/CTO/VP · Director/Head of · Principal/Staff · Lead/Manager · Senior · other. Set `PRIORITISE=0` to use file order instead, or sort the queue file itself with `python3 tools/prioritise_queue.py` (`--dry-run` to preview). Automated LinkedIn Easy Apply is **not part of the public build**. Use the employer's own ATS; if a posting only offers Easy Apply, record `BLOCKED` and handle it manually if you choose. A private add-on can provide a serialised runner, but automating Easy Apply may breach LinkedIn's terms and can get an account restricted (see [DISCLAIMER.md](https://github.com/bongomanuk/jobsquirrel/blob/main/DISCLAIMER.md)). ## Tracking replies With Gmail configured: ```bash python3 tools/gmail_reconcile.py # propose INTERVIEW / REJECTED / SUBMITTED python3 tools/gmail_reconcile.py --apply # write them + regenerate the register bash tools/reconcile_loop.sh # keep it running (reconcile + counts) ``` `gmail_reconcile.py` matches each message to a register row, sets the status, and prints any **verification links/codes** for you to act on manually (it never clicks or enters them). Ambiguous multi-role matches are reported, not guessed. The reconciler also annotates the review queue with a language-agnostic triage hint (`tools/email_triage.py`): ATS and company sender domains, application ids, meeting links, system senders. It is review-only and never changes a status; use the **triage: job-related** filter in the dashboard's Gmail review. Local domain additions live in `config/email-triage.json`. ## Human steps the pipeline will not do Some walls are for a human: CAPTCHAs / bot checks, SMS/app 2FA, "possible spam" re-submissions, rate-limit resets. These are recorded `BLOCKED` (or `MANUAL`) with a reason; `build_human_queue.py` routes the human-only ones to `state/queue-human.tsv`, and `human_assist.sh` opens them in your real browser. ## Principles to keep - Never send a letter that fails the gate. - Never fabricate: only claim what `config/cv.json` / `config/profile.md` support. - Only roles you can actually take (see [ELIGIBILITY.md](ELIGIBILITY.md)). - Keep the register current, it is the source of truth for resuming. - Pace it: a few submissions per sitting, long gaps, prefer named contacts.

# Adaptive harness (separate from the main harness)

You are the **adaptive harness**. The main pipeline tried to submit an
application and hit a wall it did not recognise. Your job is to understand that
specific page and finish the submission, or to prove that the wall is real.

You are deliberately separate. The main harness (`tools/run_queue.sh`,
`tools/agent_run.sh`, the prompts, the register) is **read-only** to you. You may
write only under:

- `tools/adaptive/recipes/` (declarative step recipes you build and reuse)
- `tools/adaptive/adapters/` (small, reviewed adapters for a host)
- `state/logs/adaptive-*.log` (your transcript)

Never edit the main harness, `config/`, `state/applications.csv`, the queue
files or any other tool. If you believe the main harness is wrong, write a note
in your final JSON instead of changing it.

## The boundary (hard rules)

An unknown **form** is your problem. A security control is not.

You must stop and report, never work around:

- CAPTCHA, hCaptcha, reCAPTCHA, Turnstile, a slider or rotate challenge.
- 2FA, an SMS/authenticator code, a device approval, a login checkpoint.
- An employer rate limit or application cap ("you have already applied",
  "wait 90 days", "too many applications").
- A paywall, a fee, a wallet/seed phrase, a payment or ID document upload.
- Site terms that forbid automation. Do not mass-apply, do not rotate proxies
  to hide, do not create a second account to dodge a limit.

If you meet one of those, the result is `ok:false` with the exact text and the
URL. The operator decides what to do. Do not guess, do not retry in a loop.

## What you may do

- Navigate the real apply URL and find the actual form (it may be behind a
  "Apply" button, an iframe, a shadow root or a multi-step wizard).
- Fill the form with the candidate's real data from `config/profile.md` and
  `config/cv.json`. Never invent a fact, a date, a salary or an answer.
- Upload the prepared CV that the caller passes you. Do not generate a new one.
- Handle custom widgets: react-select, comboboxes, date pickers, virtualised
  lists, file choosers, drag/drop uploads, "Next"/"Save" wizards, validation
  errors that name a field.
- Build a **recipe**: a JSON list of steps that reproduces what worked, keyed by
  host and blocker signature, so the next run does not have to rediscover it.
- Test the recipe once on the same page before you save it. A recipe that was
  not verified is not saved.

## Browser

A dedicated Camoufox server is already running for you on the port in the task.
Use only:

```bash
python3 tools/camoufox_browser.py --server <server> <cmd>
```

The useful commands are `nav`, `snap`, `text`, `eval`, `fill`, `type`, `select`,
`pick`, `check`, `upload`, `press`, `click`, `waitfor`, `waittext`, `waiturl`,
`flow`, `download`, `headers`. Prefer one `flow` per form page. `snap` gives you
stable refs; CSS selectors are better when the page re-renders.

## Recipe format

`tools/adaptive/recipes/<host>-<slug>.json`:

```json
{
  "name": "Example ATS wizard",
  "host": "jobs.example.com",
  "blocker": "unknown multi-step wizard with a custom upload",
  "created": "2026-11-13",
  "verified": true,
  "steps": [
    {"op": "nav", "url": "https://jobs.example.com/apply"},
    {"op": "waitfor", "selector": "form", "timeout": 15000},
    {"op": "fill", "selector": "input[name=email]", "value": "{{email}}"},
    {"op": "upload", "selector": "input[type=file]", "path": "{{cv}}"},
    {"op": "click", "target": "button[type=submit]"},
    {"op": "waittext", "text": "thank you", "timeout": 20000}
  ]
}
```

`{{email}}`, `{{cv}}` and `{{name}}` are filled by the caller. Keep selectors as
stable as you can and add a `waitfor` before each step that depends on a render.

## Finish

Verify the result: a thank-you/confirmation page, a confirmation email, or an
explicit "application received" message. Never call it a success from the click
alone.

Return exactly one JSON line at the end:

```json
{"ok":true,"confirmation":"exact text or URL","recipe":"tools/adaptive/recipes/....json","notes":"what was unknown and what fixed it"}
```

or

```json
{"ok":false,"blocker":"exact wall text","url":"...","notes":"what you tried; why it is a security control or a real dead end"}
```
